label: Fallback succession title
summary: Names a title whose holder inherits from the character when the normal line of succession finds nobody.
details: The holder of that title becomes the primary heir only in that case. Vanilla gives it the primary title of a character saved earlier as a scope.

label: Father
summary: Makes the given character the father of the character.
details: If the character had no real father separate from the previous father, the new father is treated as the real father too.

label: Figurehead title
summary: Changes whether the title is a special figurehead title.
details: The game's documentation says nothing about what a figurehead title does or which values it takes, and vanilla gives no example.

label: Focus
summary: Sets the focus the character is pursuing.
details: Vanilla writes a focus key such as `education_martial` or `martial_strategy_focus`. Twice it uses a yes/no value instead, which the input does not explain.

label: Focus progress
summary: Sets how far the character has progressed in their focus.
details: The game documents nothing more, and vanilla has no example, so the unit and range of the value are unknown.

label: Generated asexuality chance
summary: Sets the chance that a generated character is asexual.
details: The documented example writes a plain number (20); the game does not say what unit it is. Vanilla uses it once, with a named value (`asexuality_chance`).

label: Generated bisexuality chance
summary: Sets the chance that a generated character is bisexual.
details: The documented example writes a plain number (20); the game does not say what unit it is. Vanilla uses it once, with a named value (`bisexuality_chance`).

label: Generated homosexuality chance
summary: Sets the chance that a generated character is homosexual.
details: The documented example writes a plain number (20); the game does not say what unit it is. Vanilla uses it once, with a named value (`homosexuality_chance`).

label: Global variable
summary: Stores a value under a name that can be read from anywhere in the game.
details: The value can be a number, yes/no, a script value, a scope or a flag. With `days` or `years` the variable disappears after that time. It is read back with `global_var:name`. Writing only a name sets it to yes.

fields.name: name
fields.text: The name the variable is stored under.

fields.name: value
fields.text: What is stored.
fields.values: a number, yes/no, a script value, a scope or a flag (flag:x)

fields.name: days
fields.text: Removes the variable after this many days.

fields.name: years
fields.text: Removes the variable after this many years. Vanilla uses it, the game's documentation does not list it.

label: Great building
summary: Puts the named great building into the province at once and for free.
details: A great building already there may be destroyed. The owner pays nothing. To test for one, use `has_any_great_building`. Vanilla uses it mostly for the Great Wall.

label: Great building slot
summary: Adds a great building slot of the given type to the province.
details: It gives an error if the province already has a free slot. It sets the slot to that type, which may destroy existing buildings. The player can only pick buildings whose `can_construct_potential` allows it. To add a finished building without the player starting construction, use `add_great_building`.

label: Great holy war target
summary: Sets who and what a great holy war is aimed at.
details: Works on a great holy war. Vanilla gives both the target character and the target title.

fields.name: target_character
fields.text: The character that is the war's target.

fields.name: target_title
fields.text: The title that is the war's target.

label: Heritage from culture
summary: Makes the culture take its heritage from another culture.
details: The culture it runs on is changed. The culture named is only the source.

label: Holding type
summary: Changes the province's holding to another type.
details: Buildings that are not valid for the new type are removed. The game's documentation says it might also create a holding in an empty province, but that is untested.

label: Artifact to holy site
summary: Gives the artifact to a holy site as its owner.
details: The game's documentation is worded oddly (it speaks of the artifact's owner and the holy site), but vanilla's one use puts an artifact with `target = scope:relic_site`. A history entry for the change can be given, or generated automatically.

fields.name: target
fields.text: The holy site that becomes the owner.

fields.name: history
fields.text: A custom history entry for the artifact, for example to show it was stolen.

fields.name: generate_history
fields.text: Whether a history entry is generated automatically when none is given.

label: House
summary: Moves the character into the given dynasty house.
details: Vanilla mostly copies the house of a parent or of the root character.

label: House aspiration
summary: Sets the aspiration (aspect) of a dynasty house, and optionally its level.
details: Vanilla uses types such as `aspect_of_creation` and `no_aspect`, with levels 1 to 5.

fields.name: type
fields.text: Which aspiration the house gets.

fields.name: level
fields.text: The level of the aspiration. Optional.

label: House head
summary: Makes the given character the head of the house.
details: It also hands over the noble family title.

label: House name
summary: Sets the name of the dynasty house.
details: The game's documentation says the value is a dynamic description. Vanilla writes plain names such as `dynn_Wang_Goryeo`.

label: House name from dynasty
summary: Gives the house the same name as another dynasty.

label: House name from house
summary: Gives the house the same name as another house.

label: House relation
summary: Sets the relation between this house and another house.
details: Run on one house, with the other house as `target`. Vanilla uses levels such as `feud`, `quarrel` and `friendly`.

fields.name: target
fields.text: The other house.

fields.name: type
fields.text: The kind of relation.

fields.name: level
fields.text: How good or bad the relation becomes.
fields.values: a relation level, such as feud, quarrel or friendly

fields.name: description
fields.text: The text that says why the latest change happened.
fields.values: a localization key or dynamic description

fields.name: save_scope_as
fields.text: Saves the relation under a name for later use.

label: Immortal age
summary: Changes the age at which the character became immortal.
details: It only works if the character is already immortal. The documented example uses 20.

label: Important location
summary: Marks the county as important to a higher title, and fires an event or on_action when it enters or leaves that title's realm.
details: In those events, root is the top liege of the title, `scope:county` is the county and `scope:title` is the interested title. `scope:changed_top_liege` is the former top liege when entering, and the new one when leaving. Vanilla uses it with the Roman empire titles and one yearly emperor event.

fields.name: title
fields.text: The higher title that is interested in the county.

fields.name: enter_realm_event
fields.text: Event fired when the county enters that title's realm.

fields.name: enter_realm_on_action
fields.text: On_action fired when the county enters that title's realm.

fields.name: leave_realm_event
fields.text: Event fired when the county leaves that title's realm.

fields.name: leave_realm_on_action
fields.text: On_action fired when the county leaves that title's realm.

label: Influence level
summary: Sets the character's influence level to the given value.
details: The game documents nothing more, and vanilla gives no example, so the allowed values are unknown.

label: Killer is public
summary: Makes the killer of the character publicly known.
details: Vanilla only writes `yes`.

label: Knight status
summary: Sets whether the character is a knight: forced, default or disallowed.
details: Vanilla writes `force`, `forbid` and `default`.

label: Child: known bastard
summary: Makes the child of the current pregnancy a known bastard, or an unknown one.
details: Only works while the character is pregnant. Vanilla always writes `yes`.

label: Landless title
summary: Sets whether the title is landless, so rulers with no land can hold it.

label: Language from culture
summary: Makes the culture take its language from another culture.
details: The culture it runs on is changed. The culture named is only the source.

label: Leading house
summary: Makes the given house the leading house of the confederation.

label: Legend chapter
summary: Sets the text of one named chapter of the legend.
details: Vanilla uses chapter names such as `discovery`, `battle`, `motivation` and `conclusion`.

fields.name: name
fields.text: Which chapter.
fields.values: a chapter name, such as opening, battle or conclusion

fields.name: localization_key
fields.text: The text the chapter gets.

label: Legend property
summary: Sets the object stored under a named property of the legend.
details: Vanilla sets properties like `ancestor` and `location`.

fields.name: name
fields.text: The property to set.

fields.name: target
fields.text: The object it is set to.
fields.values: a scope, such as a character or a province

label: Legend quality
summary: Sets the quality of the legend.
details: The game's documentation lists famed, illustrious and mythical.

label: Local variable
summary: Stores a value under a name as a local variable.
details: The game's documentation is the one for `set_variable` and does not explain what makes a variable local. Going by its name, it is read back with `local_var:name`. Vanilla writes it with a name and a value, mostly `yes` or small numbers.

fields.name: name
fields.text: The name the variable is stored under.

fields.name: value
fields.text: What is stored.
fields.values: a number, yes/no, a script value, a scope or a flag

fields.name: days
fields.text: Removes the variable after this many days.

label: Location
summary: Moves the character to the given province.
details: With `stick_to_location = yes`, the game's safety checks do not send the character back to their default location.

fields.name: location
fields.text: The province to move to.

fields.name: stick_to_location
fields.text: Keeps the game from returning the character to their default location.

label: Default location
summary: Moves the character back to their default location.
details: That is usually the realm capital for a landed character, or the court location for a courtier.

label: Main rite
summary: Makes the rite the main one of its faith.

label: Martial custom from culture
summary: Makes the culture take its martial custom from another culture.
details: The culture it runs on is changed. The culture named is only the source.

label: Maximum durability
summary: Sets the artifact's maximum durability.
details: Vanilla uses numbers such as 25, 40 and 50.
